proposal.rationale: Both allowlisted PQC-capable profiles (tls13-mlkem768 and tls13-hybrid-x25519-mlkem768) are implementable via liboqs-0.16.0, which is present on the asset. Checking peer readiness/capabilities: peer-01 and peer-02 only advertise kem:x25519 (no PQC capability, so not ready for either PQC profile). peer-03 is 'known' and advertises both kem:x25519mlkem768 and kem:mlkem768, making it a ready endpoint for both PQC profiles. peer-04 advertises kem:x25519mlkem768 (ready for the hybrid profile) but per Engineering Notes it is scheduled for decommissioning and must be excluded from this batch regardless of technical readiness. Consequently, both PQC profiles yield the same maximum of 1 ready, in-batch endpoint (peer-03). Per policy, when candidate profiles tie on endpoint count, the higher security class is preferred: security_class_order ranks 'pqc' above 'hybrid-pqc'. Therefore tls13-mlkem768 is selected. This satisfies the hybrid-pqc security floor (pqc exceeds it) and does not repeat the asset's current profile (tls13-x25519, classical). No peer has unconfirmed readiness, so there are no unresolved dependencies; peer-01/peer-02 are simply capability-ineligible and peer-04 is deliberately excluded per the decommissioning note. Execution should occur within the Tuesday 02:00-04:00 UTC change window with the on-call network team as rollback owner, monitoring handshake error rates for 30 minutes post-change per the change window note.
